title: Pieces out of play

D0.outcome: Explains that a piece can be out of play (shut in or far from the action) without being capturable.

D1.outcome: Finds the piece cut off from the action in a given position and says what cuts it off.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, classifies a piece as out of play, able to get out, or really trapped, and plans either to keep an enemy piece cut off or to free his own.

D3.outcome: Counts the cost of freeing a shut-in piece (a lever, an exchange) against the benefit of playing on the other wing while the enemy piece is idle.

misconceptions: A shut-in piece is a lost piece.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §3 (POS.OUTOFPLAY as the contrast with TAC.TRAPPED)
conditions: The cut-off piece cannot be freed except at a cost.
contrasts: The piece can be freed by a sacrifice or an exchange.
Treating a temporarily blocked piece as lost without checking the defender's counter-sacrifices.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.EXCHANGE.D1: trading off the guard of the exit frees the piece
